title: PDF FPV Drones Strike Tada-U Air Force Base, Damaging Jets and Shutting Mandalay International Airport
detail: Around 2:00 p.m. on September 10, 2026, People's Defence Force fighters launched six first-person-view (FPV) 'suicide' drones at the military air base within the compound of Tada-U International Airport, roughly 35km south of Mandalay. Resistance sources said the strike damaged four jets, including a direct hit on a Yak-130's nose, while the junta said all drones were intercepted before causing damage. A PDF spokesperson said the attack targeted only the section of the base housing aircraft that have been conducting airstrikes on civilians. Mandalay International Airport, which shares the site, was closed for two days (September 10-12) as a result, disrupting flights and forcing residents of seven nearby villages to flee amid the military's response.

media.caption: Aerial view of Tada-U Air Force Base, Mandalay Region, following the September 10 FPV drone attack.

title: Retreating Junta Column Kills Five Civilians Including 90-Year-Old Man Near Wedi Village, Launglon Township
detail: On the morning of September 10, 2026, a Myanmar military column retreating from Wedi village in Launglon Township, Tanintharyi Region, killed five civilians, including a man over 90 years old near Kone Zayat village and three other displaced people from Mae Maw village. A local source suggested the killings may have been retaliation for military losses in fighting the previous day, though this has not been independently corroborated.

media.caption: MoeMaKa CDM domestic news digest reporting the September 10 killings near Wedi village, Launglon Township.
